# Separate Demo B's single-window tear-out gesture driver

## Context

Next bounded continuation of #15614. The parent asks for discoverable responsibilities and smaller reading/review/merge surfaces, not merely fewer state owners. The [corrected peer read](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/15614#issuecomment-6700401406) keeps that intent live: the lack of a safe Engine Workspace scheduler adoption does not retire the original raw-line target.

The cross-window gesture, keyboard and native routing slices are already separate or approved. This leaf separates the remaining single-window tear-out driver.

## The Problem

At `8efc2c653b`, `DemoBWorkspace.mjs` still contains a 197-line `executeTearOutStep` among native ownership and projection methods. Together with its five observation/cancellation helpers it occupies 249 method lines, before JSDoc. A change to the demo's arm → boundary exit → actual birth → survival moves → commit/cancel sequence still requires reading and editing the composition host.

This family has its own reason to change and validation surface: `DemoBDockTearOutNL.spec.mjs` and the Engine matrix call the existing executor. Separating it improves navigation and review locality without inventing another lifecycle.

## The Architectural Reality

- `examples/dashboard/crossWindow/DemoBWorkspace.mjs:1438–1785` contains the driver and helpers, interleaved with runtime identity helpers that stay on the host.
- Move exactly `executeTearOutStep`, `waitForTearOutDragArmed`, `hasTearOutVessel`, `waitForTearOutVessel`, `waitForTearOutCommit`, and `cancelTearOutGesture`.
- `exactTearOutVessel` and `resolveVesselKey` remain host-side, as do the Group records, pane cache, interaction service, projection queue, commit/native effects and destruction.
- The six bodies are identical on current `origin/dev df66128496` and the approved native-host candidate. This is independent of that slice's six routing methods.
- The existing `DemoBCrossWindowGesture` / `DemoBKeyboardHost` Base prototype mixins establish the same-owner pattern. A second constructed driver, controller, registry or callback bundle is unnecessary.

Design authority: n/a — preserves existing behavior while fulfilling the parent's maintenance outcome.

Prescription checked: `examples/dashboard/crossWindow/DemoBCrossWindowGesture.mjs` — the demo-local driver is the owning layer; independent source inspection identified this cohesive sequence and its existing native consumers. Generic `src/draggable` policy and Workstation controller integration are different concerns.

## The Fix

Add `examples/dashboard/crossWindow/DemoBTearOutGesture.mjs` as a registered Base prototype mixin and compose it into the workspace.

Retain `executeTearOutStep(step, options)` and `waitForTearOutCommit(itemId, sourceNodeId, options)` as small host facades supplying the main workspace ID to distinctly named internal implementations. Preserve their default options, promises and result shapes. Other moved methods remain callable on the host through the mixin. Do not import DemoBWorkspace back into its mixin.

Internal calls continue resolving current host methods/collaborators after waits. Preserve arming readiness, actual Group-observed birth, post-birth movement, exact commit/cancel receipts, and Escape-before-mouseup cleanup. Delete the moved implementations from the host.

## Contract Ledger

| Surface | Authority | Preserved behavior | Refusal/fallback | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `executeTearOutStep(step, options)` | Existing host and `DemoBDockTearOutNL` | Same async receipt, defaults and live host calls; real single-window boundary grammar | Existing invalid-step, unavailable-surface, failed-admission and cancellation outcomes | Method comparison; existing native birth/commit/cancel/middle-tab journeys |
| Observation/poll helpers | Current Group records, document truth and host `waitFor` | Same readiness and bounded polling; no copied registry or second timer owner | Existing false/refusal results | Existing units and native journeys |
| `cancelTearOutGesture` | Current interaction service and drag-zone contract | Escape dispatch settles before mouseup; current collaborator lookup | Existing missing-button receipt and caller cleanup | Existing cancellation/blocked-acquisition matrix controls |
| Host composition/lifetime | Current workspace, staging module and Group | Fields, native routing, document commits, projection and destruction stay put | Existing generation/retirement fences | Existing workspace/lifecycle suite |

Decision Record impact: aligned-with `neomjs/neo#adr:docking-design` §2.3; no policy or protocol change.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The six-method family has one discoverable demo-local home; old implementations are removed, public host entry points retained, and no independent state/lifecycle owner added.
- [ ] Method bodies remain behavior-equivalent except explicit semantic-ID parameters and distinct internal names; defaults, live dispatch, refusal and cancellation order remain intact.
- [ ] Existing DemoBWorkspace/TourRunner units and full Engine unit suite pass without weakened expectations. Add a focused control only for a named gap the move exposes.
- [ ] Headed `DemoBDockTearOutNL` and Engine matrix rows 5/7 pass on the candidate, preserving pane identity, document outcomes and terminal cleanup. Record environment and exact run scope separately from hosted CI.
- [ ] Contextual JSDoc/`@summary` is preserved; report host/module raw and code-line counts, lower the existing size ratchet, and reconcile the parent phase map without claiming its original raw target or all remaining phases complete.

## Out of Scope

Changing gesture thresholds, popup acquisition policy, generic drag machinery, Workstation controllers, projection scheduling, perspectives, tour script/content, or the existing native-host routing slice. No `_from` collision-guard repair. No invented third-party/fleet acceptance or parent closure.

## Avoided Traps

Do not enlarge the already 989-line cross-window gesture module. This is a separate, independently exercised single-window sequence. Do not move adjacent `exactTearOutVessel` / `resolveVesselKey` merely because they interrupt its text range. A mixin can overwrite a same-named facade, so internal runner/poller names must differ. Do not replace current host lookups with captured construction snapshots.

## Ownership and freshness

Sophie owns this already-planned parent continuation; it is not a standalone contributor intake. Structural fast-path: same Body example directory and lifecycle role as the existing gesture and keyboard mixins. No Agent OS structure-map command applies.
